Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

elorian sciencevision · benchmark task: ScienceVision compares native-file source access, source access plus MCP inspection tools, and a fixed six-rendered-view control; MCP tools permit changing views, isolating structures, navigating slices and measuring geometry.

candidate.next12.sciencevision.access-conditions.v3

  • The settings use the same underlying artifacts but provide different information and interactions. Public webpage viewers are described as expert-facing demonstrations rather than the evaluation harness.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

elorian sciencevision · evaluates: The ScienceVision article describes mean answer scores on a zero-to-one scale, counting ineligible trials as zero, averaging available repeats within each question and then across the 250 questions.

candidate.next12.sciencevision.aggregation.v2

  • The source discloses unequal repeat counts for some configurations and different scaffolds for GPT versus other models. Neither uniform three-repeat coverage nor model-only causation is inferred.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

elorian sciencevision · documents: ScienceVision’s creators caution that a correct answer under native-source access can result from direct computation over the artifact and is not by itself evidence of successful visual observation.

candidate.next12.sciencevision.observation-limit.v2

  • The interactive webpage converts two demonstration artifacts, including CT resampling; those demonstrations are not treated as byte-identical native evaluation inputs.
  • The full manuscript, native files, interactive sessions, task payloads and reuse rights were not independently audited.

Approved evidence · As of 12 Nov 2026

elorian sciencevision · dataset size: ScienceVision’s creator article describes 250 expert-level questions, 50 each in biology, chemistry, medical imaging, mechanical CAD and architecture, across 22 subdomains, paired with native scientific artifacts and task-specific reference answers.

candidate.next12.sciencevision.units.v2

  • The article defines expert-level by domain knowledge and conventions, not a human-difficulty baseline. Domains and access settings do not create additional benchmark families.
